title: Atomic Physics and X-rays — 40 MCQs
description: Covers Bohr’s theory of the hydrogen atom, spectral series, excitation and ionization potentials, energy levels, emission and absorption spectra, de Broglie theory and wave-particle duality, the uncertainty principle, nature and production of X-rays, and Bragg’s law.

questions.explanation: Bohr’s quantization condition states that mvr = nh/2π where n = 1, 2, 3, …

questions.q: The energy of the electron in the ground state of hydrogen is
questions.explanation: E₁ = −13.6 eV for the n = 1 level of hydrogen.

questions.q: The ionization potential of the hydrogen atom is
questions.explanation: Ionization energy from the ground state is 13.6 eV, so the ionization potential is 13.6 V.

questions.q: The Lyman series of hydrogen lies in the
questions.explanation: All Lyman lines (transitions to n = 1) fall in the ultraviolet.

questions.explanation: Balmer lines (transitions to n = 2) appear in the visible spectrum.

questions.q: de Broglie’s relation for the wavelength of a particle is
questions.explanation: The de Broglie wavelength is λ = h/p where p is the momentum of the particle.

questions.explanation: The product of uncertainties in position and momentum is at least h/4π.

questions.explanation: X-rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths typically 0.01–10 nm.

questions.q: X-rays are produced when
options: fast electrons strike a metal target
questions.explanation: In an X-ray tube accelerated electrons hit a metal anode and produce X-rays.

questions.q: Bragg’s law for X-ray diffraction is
questions.explanation: Constructive interference occurs when 2d sinθ = nλ where d is the interplanar spacing.

The energy required to excite a hydrogen atom from the ground state to the second excited state is
questions.explanation: Second excited state is n = 3; E₃ = −13.6/9 ≈ −1.51 eV; ΔE = 13.6 − 1.51 = 12.09 eV.

questions.q: The longest wavelength in the Lyman series is
questions.explanation: Longest λ corresponds to the smallest energy jump (n = 2 → n = 1): λ = 121.6 nm.

questions.q: An electron and a photon have the same de Broglie wavelength. The ratio of their kinetic energies (electron to photon) is
questions.explanation: For the electron KE = p²/2m = h²/(2m λ²); for the photon E = pc = hc/λ. Thus KE_e / E_ph = h/(2m c λ) < 1 for typical wavelengths.

questions.q: The minimum energy of an electron that can produce characteristic K-series X-rays of a target with K-shell binding energy 70 keV is
questions.explanation: The incident electron must have kinetic energy at least equal to the binding energy of the K-shell electron in order to eject it.

questions.explanation: Moseley’s law states that √ν = a(Z − b); the plot of √ν against atomic number Z is a straight line.

questions.explanation: E₃ − E₁ = −1.51 − (−13.6) = 12.09 eV ≈ 12.1 eV, so the electron reaches n = 3.

questions.explanation: In the Bohr model KE = −E_total, so KE / E_total = −1.

questions.explanation: The series limit is the shortest wavelength, arising from the transition n = ∞ → n = 2.
